Just a heads up but "net worth" can be an extremely misleading way to define someone's financial status. For example, if you own a property that's worth $100,000 and you put 3.5% down to buy it, so $3500. you have the remaining balance of $96,500 as debt. Since your net worth is your equity minus your liability (cash/value minus debt) you would actually have a negative net worth in that scenario. However, you also now control an appreciating asset worth $100,000 that you just leveraged with $3,500 so it's actually a very smart play - especially If you put roommates in it to pay down your mortgage. Now you're in a scenario where you are just taking on debt and having others pay it off. What I'm trying to say here is that having a lot of debt doesn't mean you're broke and using debt is actually the fastest way to achieve exponential growth. Also, net worth and liquidity aren't the same thing. If we take that same $100,000 home and some time has gone by and you have $25,000 worth of equity in it that adds to your net worth. So your net worth has gone up $25,000 but the only way you can touch the equity is if you do a Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC) and borrow against the equity (with an interest rate of course) or you sell the home (you can sell your home to buy another property; residential or otherwise and not pay taxes if you use a 1031 exchange).
